Subject: Re: Fwd: EastAsia edge onboarding & initial sizing ask

Thanks for the context and the workbook — looked through the calc. High level responses:

1) Sizing: under the assumptions (13B model, ~280 tokens total, batching ~20), steady-state of 1200 req/min maps to ~60 concurrent requests sustained; with bursts to 3000/min we hit ~150 concurrent. For our optimized runtime on A100-equivalent edge nodes (quantized), rough GPU mapping is:
- Sustained lane: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs (shared across pool, high-util batching)
- Burst lane (elastic): add 6 x A100-equivalent pre-warmed instances available for immediate failover (autoscaler + warm spare strategy)
- Buffer: 2 x smaller instances for quick cold-start traffic absorb

That yields a pilot footprint of ~12 GPU-equivalents total (with autoscaling policies). Exact instance types will depend on partner colo availability.

2) Lead time: provisioning dedicated nodes in Tokyo typically 6 weeks if we have vendor stock; if we need new capacity ordering it's 10–12 weeks. Because the timeline is tight for Feb 1, we should negotiate a hybrid plan: start pilot on reserved shared-hosted edge with dedicated routing (fastest) for month 0–1, then migrate to dedicated pool by month 2. That reduces risk to the Feb start.

3) Ops notes: KV cache warm-up will be a critical factor for p95. Recommend a small staged traffic ramp (10% increments over 48–72 hours) and pre-warm cache using synthetic traffic.

I'll add comments in the spreadsheet. Happy to join a call with EastBridge to walk the technical plan.

—Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference
